newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Fergie says former lover Bryan beat her.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Fergie says former lover Bryan beat her.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York said in an interview published on Sunday that her former lover, John Bryan had beaten her black and blue in a fit of rage after she refused to show him her diary.

The duchess, who last May divorced Prince Andrew, Queen Elizabeth's second son, told the Independent on Sunday that the attack took place in March 1995 after a dinner party when Bryan, a balding Texan, tore up her diary and threw it around the room.

"I wouldn't let him look at it. He hit me. I had bruises all down my arms because I held them up to defend myself. I don't think any woman in the world likes to be hit and I certainly don't," said the 36-year-old duchess, formerly Sarah Ferguson.
The interview was one of several the duchess, known as Fergie, has given recently to publicise her autobiography "My Story", which paints an unflattering picture of Britain's royal family.

Any affection that the British public might have had for Fergie vanished in 1992 when a newspaper published photos of her frolicking topless in the south of France with Bryan, her "financial adviser" who appeared to be sucking her toes.
The duchess said the queen offered kindness and support during her difficulties -- and still does.

"We talk to each other. I love her. I love her to bits," flame-haired Fergie said. But Prince Philip, the queen's husband, sent "incredibly cruel" letters accusing her of letting down the royal family through her wayward behaviour.

Tantalisingly, Fergie hinted that reconciliation with Andrew might be on the cards. "Yes, we could still get back together," she was quoted as saying. Pressed to elaborate, she added: "I'm not sure whether I should say any more."
